# Issue with `create_code_verifier` in OAuth2 Client

The `create_code_verifier` method in the OAuth2 Client class is not generating valid code verifiers according to the PKCE specification.

When trying to use the PKCE flow with the client, the code verifier generation fails validation:

```python
from oauthlib.oauth2 import Client

client = Client("my_client_id")
code_verifier = client.create_code_verifier(length=96)
# Trying to use this code_verifier fails
```

The issue appears to be in the regex pattern and token generation in the `create_code_verifier` method:

https://github.com/oauthlib/oauthlib/blob/master/oauthlib/oauth2/rfc6749/clients/base.py#L490-L494

The code verifier should only contain characters from the set [A-Za-z0-9-._~] as per the PKCE spec, but the current implementation:

1. Has an incorrect regex pattern (`^[A-Zaa-z0-9-._~]` instead of `^[A-Za-z0-9-._~]`)
2. Uses `secrets.token_urlsafe()` which generates tokens with characters that may not match the required character set

To reproduce:

```python
from oauthlib.oauth2 import Client

# Create a client
client = Client("test_client")

# Generate a code verifier
code_verifier = client.create_code_verifier(length=96)

# Check if it matches the required pattern
import re
allowed_characters = re.compile('^[A-Za-z0-9-._~]+$')
print(re.search(allowed_characters, code_verifier))  # This returns None, indicating failure

# Try to create a code challenge
try:
    challenge = client.create_code_challenge(code_verifier)
    print("Challenge created:", challenge)
except ValueError as e:
    print("Error:", e)  # This will show the error
```
